strict_rationale: Flipped true by TC-695 (G3/REQ-G3-011), 2026-11-06: no automated, unattended path in this repository runs this file's conformance test with FOSS_MCP_CONFORMANCE_EXHAUSTIVE=1 and strict enforcement together (confirmed by grepping .github/workflows/, ops/*.py, and every other automation entrypoint for FOSS_MCP_CONFORMANCE_EXHAUSTIVE -- the only hits are this module's own docstrings/comments, other tests' comments, taskcard yaml investigation text, and a historical ops/instructions.jsonl rework record; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs tests/conformance in default mode only, with FOSS_MCP_CONFORMANCE_EXHAUSTIVE unset). Under default mode (the only mode CI ever exercises), every remaining known_failures entry was directly re-measured to still reproduce exactly (confirmed: after removing the 104 entries this same commit prunes, default-mode observed failures equal known_failures exactly -- zero stale, zero new). The known residual risk is case-(g) (bare-namespace-word-false-exact/bare-member-word-false-exact): its case_id is computed from a sample-order-dependent probe word that differs between default and exhaustive mode, so a future EXHAUSTIVE run under this now-strict baseline will spuriously flag those entries as stale even though they are still genuinely broken -- but since no automated path runs exhaustive mode, that false alarm, if it ever fires, only ever reaches a human running it manually, who would review it before acting. If an automated/unattended exhaustive run is ever added, re-flip this to false first, or fix case-(g)'s identity-stability in _measure_pilot (tracked as a separate, future card) before relying on strict there.
